Hi Susan — great to hear (and thanks for the clear ask). I’ve looped in Marissa from Finance and Rachel on Sales Ops to help with credit and paperwork. Below is a practical proposal we can execute quickly: 

- Net terms: Net60 for the first 6-month committed term (subject to on-time payment on first two invoices).
- Invoicing cadence: Three pro-forma invoices per quarter (Start: 40% deposit, Mid: 30%, End: 30%). We propose the first invoice be due in 60 days from issue; the deposit invoice can be issued immediately to reserve capacity if you prefer shorter timing.
- Credit limit: We can provision a provisional credit limit tied to the committed spend (we’ll confirm the exact cap after a quick finance review).
- VAT: Redwood will include your VAT ID, show net/gross line items, and include the standard EU reverse-charge statement on the invoice PDF. I’m attaching a short guidance doc that Finance uses for EU customers.

Action items I propose:
1) Marissa to run a credit-quick-check (should take <48 hours).
2) Rachel to prepare the pro-forma invoices (attached draft) and DocuSign purchase order if needed.
3) Susan/Pieter to confirm whether you want the 40% as immediate deposit or Net60.

If that works I’ll lock it in and Marissa will reach out with credit details.

Thanks —
Jonas

- First two invoices must be paid within agreed terms to keep Net60; one late payment will require moving to Net30 and/or requiring a deposit for subsequent invoices.
- For EU reverse-charge customers, we require a validated VAT ID on the signed order form and we will include the reverse-charge annotation verbatim on the invoice.
- If MedAxis prefers 0% upfront, we’ll require trade-credit insurance or a shortened payment term as an alternative.

I’ve attached the pro-forma with the VAT annotation and a checklist of required fields for AP (billing address, VAT ID, PO#). Please confirm whether the first invoice should be issued immediately (40% deposit) or on Net60.

If you confirm immediate deposit, we’ll issue Invoice #RDW-PRO-001 today.
